meta.description: Online gold-ring buying checklist. Each item shows whether its underlying rule is anchored to an official source (fetched 2026-10-22) or is prudent-practice advice.

checklist.item: Gold purity — confirm the karat (10K, 14K, 18K...). Higher karat = more gold.
checklist.source_label: 16 CFR §23.3 — karat fineness must be correctly disclosed
checklist.detail: Karat = parts of gold per 24. 18K = 75.0%, 14K = 58.3%, 10K = 41.7%. See the Gold Prices & Karats page for the full table.

checklist.item: Solid gold — listing must explicitly say SOLID gold — not plated, vermeil, gold-filled, gold overlay, or gold-tone.
checklist.source_label: 16 CFR §23.3(b)(3),(5)-(8), (c)(1)-(2) — plated/filled/overlay terms are surface coatings with their own fineness rules; hollow pieces may not be called 'solid'
checklist.detail: Vermeil = gold-plated silver. Gold-filled/rolled gold plate = mechanically bonded surface layer (≥1/40th of article weight at ≥10K for the mechanical plating example in the Guides). If a listing can't say 'solid 14K gold' or 'solid 18K gold', walk away.

checklist.item: Hallmark — look for a 10K/14K/18K stamp PLUS a maker's/manufacturer's mark.
checklist.source_label: eCFR §23.10 quoting the National Stamping Act (15 U.S.C. §297)
checklist.detail: '...who applies or causes to be applied a quality mark... shall apply to the article the trademark or name of such person.' A karat stamp with NO maker's mark is a red flag. UK-sold rings carry independent assay-office hallmarks (e.g. London, hallmarking since 1300).

checklist.item: Weight — check the ring's weight in grams. A legitimate seller should be able to provide it.
checklist.source_label: Project checklist; supported by 16 CFR §23.18 (weight misrepresentation is deceptive)
checklist.detail: FINDING: none of the 14 listings reviewed publishes metal weight in grams (see Flag F1). Request it in writing; use the calculator page to convert weight + karat into metal value.

checklist.item: Seller reputation — research independent reviews and complaints; verify real contact information.
checklist.detail: Also verify corporate changes: e.g. James Allen now routes to Blue Nile (Flag F8) — know exactly WHICH legal entity you are buying from. US sellers operating deceptively on metal content face FTC Act §5 enforcement via the Jewelry Guides.

checklist.item: Price — compare the price with the ring's gold weight and current gold value. Unusually cheap = red flag.
checklist.source_label: Project checklist; anchor price on Gold Prices page (World Gold Council, fetched 2026-10-22)
checklist.detail: Use the calculator: metal melt value = grams × (karat/24) × spot-per-gram. Retail settings are priced far above melt (design, brand, labour, stones) — but BELOW-melt pricing on a 'gold' ring is a classic fake signal.

checklist.item: Return policy — make sure you can return it after receiving and inspecting it; check exclusions on resized/custom rings.
checklist.source_label: Project checklist; compare with retailer policies found
checklist.detail: Verified examples 2026-10-22: Mejuri free 30-day returns & exchanges; Blue Nile free returns; Cartier complimentary returns & exchanges; Brilliant Earth free shipping & returns + free 1-year resizing; Tiffany — CONFLICTING text flagged (F2): confirm in writing before buying. Engraving/resizing often final-sale (Mejuri engraving: not eligible for returns).

checklist.item: Payment — prefer a credit card for purchase protection; avoid irreversible payment methods.
checklist.detail: Irreversible methods (wire, crypto, gift cards) leave no chargeback path. Note: financing plans seen on listings (Affirm/Klarna/Blue Nile card) are credit products, not purchase protection.

checklist.item: Documentation — keep the listing, receipt, description, and the seller's claims about gold purity.
checklist.detail: Screenshot the listing including any 'solid 14K/18K gold' wording — the FTC Guides make metal-content claims part of the product's lawful description, so your record is your evidence.

checklist.item: Upon arrival — before wearing or resizing, take it to an independent jeweler to verify gold purity and weight.
checklist.detail: Do this INSIDE the return window. Resizing before verification can forfeit your return rights (see C7 exclusions).

checklist.item: Best verification — ask for XRF testing or another professional purity test; don't rely on the stamp.
checklist.source_label: Project checklist; independent assay is the job of assay offices (e.g. London Assay Office)
checklist.detail: XRF (X-ray fluorescence) reads surface composition non-destructively; fire assay is destructive but definitive. A stamp is only a claim — 15 U.S.C. §294 makes FALSE marks unlawful, but enforcement happens after the fact; test the piece.

checklist.item: If the seller won't let you independently verify/return it — don't buy.
checklist.detail: This is the project's bright line. A confident seller of real solid gold has nothing to fear from a jeweler's scale and an XRF read.

key_principle: A 14K or 18K stamp by itself does NOT prove purity. The safe pattern: reputable seller + correct markings (karat + maker's mark) + price consistent with weight × karat × spot + independent testing after delivery.

key_principle_sources.label: 15 U.S.C. ch. 8 — National Gold and Silver Stamping Act
Gold spot anchor — World Gold Council
